description: Unauthorized Access to Game Analytics Data via API Gateway Attackers might attempt to forge Cognito tokens, exploit token validation bugs, or use stolen credentials to gain unauthorized access to the API endpoints. An attacker obtains valid credentials through phishing or token theft, then uses these to submit falsified game analytics data that could skew business metrics or game balance decisions.
references: recommendation: Implement mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication for API Gateway endpoints
recommendation: Enhance Cognito user pool security settings

description: Data Exposure in S3 Buckets Misconfigured bucket policies, overly permissive IAM roles, or accidentally disabled block public access settings could expose sensitive game analytics data. An attacker discovers a misconfigured S3 bucket policy that allows listing of objects, downloads sensitive game analytics data, and uses it for competitive analysis or to expose player behavior patterns.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Enhance S3 bucket security configurations

description: Kinesis Stream Data Interception Insufficient encryption of data in transit or overly permissive IAM policies could allow unauthorized access to real-time game analytics data streams. An attacker with access to the AWS network infrastructure could potentially intercept or modify game analytics data as it flows between services.
references: recommendation: Enable encryption for all Kinesis streams
recommendation: Implement strict IAM policies for Kinesis access

description: EMR Cluster Security Compromise Attackers could exploit vulnerabilities in EMR applications, misconfigured security groups, or weak SSH access controls to gain unauthorized access to the cluster. An attacker gains access to the EMR cluster through a misconfigured security group, then uses this access to manipulate data processing jobs or access sensitive data.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1499 - Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Implement comprehensive EMR security controls

description: DynamoDB Game State Manipulation Attackers could exploit overly permissive IAM policies or vulnerabilities in the processing Lambda to manipulate game state data in DynamoDB. An attacker compromises the processing Lambda function and uses its permissions to modify game state data, potentially affecting game balance or player progress.
references: recommendation: Implement strict access controls for DynamoDB
recommendation: Enable advanced DynamoDB security features
